行政長官李家超今到立法會參與首場「對談交流會」，會後與立法會主席李慧琼會見傳媒。李家超回應宏福苑長遠居住安排時，指已有 53％ 業主簽訂買賣協議，籲住戶「把握時間作決定」。 他另回應陳嘉信涉司法抄襲被提早退休事件，指尊重首席法官採適當措施，維護公眾對法官獨立專業履責的信心。至於黃錦輝涉醉駕請辭而空缺的議席，會否進行補選，李家超指未來 18 個月有三場重要選舉，認為在時間、工作、相對必要性方面，應先做好這三場選舉。

Chief Executive John Lee today attended the first 'Exchange and Dialogue Session' at the Legislative Council, and met the media with LegCo President Starry Lee afterwards. When responding to questions about the long-term accommodation arrangements for Wang Fuk Court, Lee said that 53% of owners had signed sale and purchase agreements, and urged residents to "seize the time to make a decision." He also responded to the matter of Judge Jonathan Man SC being required to retire early over allegations of judicial plagiarism, saying he respected the Chief Justice's taking of appropriate measures to maintain public confidence in the independent and professional fulfilment of duties by judges. As to whether a by-election will be held for the seat vacated by Wong Kim-fai's resignation over a drink-driving charge, Lee pointed out that there will be three important elections in the coming 18 months, and believed that in terms of timing, workload and relative necessity, priority should be given to ensuring the smooth conduct of these three elections.

53% of owners have signed sale and purchase agreements; nearly 91% have signed acceptance letters for the acquisition

When asked about the progress of the acquisition of Wang Fuk Court, and whether the authorities had inquired into the reasons of residents who had not yet signed the consent forms, Lee said the matter had been handled throughout with 'compassion, reason and the law', reiterating that for the long-term accommodation arrangements, the government was acquiring the property rights at a price of HK$8,000 to HK$10,500 per square foot, and was also bearing various risks, including the uncertainty of insurance compensation and the risk of possible involvement in different legal proceedings.

He said that as of yesterday, 90.8% of owners had signed letters accepting the acquisition proposal and 53% had completed signing the sale and purchase agreements, with owners also progressively completing the formal assignment of title, describing the process as smooth and saying he 'hopes everyone will seize the time to make a decision.' He also pointed out that the decision is of course to be made by each household based on their own actual circumstances, but as to the acquisition price, the bearing of risks and the provision of other assistance, '[we] hope to let the households concerned make a decision as soon as possible, and hope everyone can return to normal life at an early date'. He also said some flats would be put up very soon for residents to consider, 'this opportunity – everyone should grab it as early as possible, as there is a chance to apply for a long-term residence unit that suits your wishes'.

Lee also reiterated that the government had recently improved the rental subsidy arrangements, and that the Legislative Council had approved a funding application of HK$1 billion for the acquisition of Wang Chi Court, adding that it would continue to do a good job in explaining the matter, and that households with questions or requests could convey them to the explanation team or their dedicated social worker, and that the matter would be handled flexibly and pragmatically in accordance with actual circumstances.

Asked about the long-term accommodation arrangements for Wang Fuk Court, Lee said 53% of owners had signed sale and purchase agreements, with some owners having already completed the assignment of title, describing the process as smooth.

Responding to Jonathan Man being forced into early retirement over plagiarism: respects the Chief Justice's taking of appropriate measures

As to the fact that Mr Justice Jonathan Man of the Court of First Instance of the High Court was found to have plagiarised on multiple occasions, and was required by Chief Justice Andrew Cheung to retire early yesterday, when asked whether this was sufficient to restore public confidence, Lee said the community has high expectations of judges and of professional standards, and that the Judiciary has always operated and managed its affairs independently. He said he respected the Chief Justice's taking of appropriate measures to maintain public confidence in the independent and professional fulfilment of duties by judges, and expressed confidence that judges and judicial officers at all levels of the courts would abide by their judicial oaths and discharge their judicial duties with diligence, independence and professionalism.

The High Court judge involved in the judicial plagiarism case, Mr Justice Jonathan Man, has been required to retire early; the Chief Executive responded today by saying he respected the Chief Justice's taking of appropriate measures to maintain public confidence. (File photo)

Separately, the University of Hong Kong's President Xiang Zhang, who was previously embroiled in a controversy over campus governance, said yesterday that he would step down in 2028 upon completing two terms totalling 10 years. When asked how he assessed Zhang's performance, and whether he would require HKU to add terms requiring the new president to maintain good communication with the Council when recruiting a successor, Lee said that Zhang, as a scientist who loves science, was eager to return to the laboratory to solve scientific problems and contribute to society. He thanked Zhang for giving early notice of his decision to the University Council, allowing the university sufficient time to recruit a new president.

Lee also thanked Zhang for his hard work and contributions to HKU during his past and future tenure as president. He said the work of recruiting a new president would be handled by the University Council, pointing out that each university has a well-functioning mechanism for appointing its president, and expressing confidence that the Council would handle the task well, and that it could be ensured that the new president would lead HKU in continued development and progress.

HKU President Xiang Zhang announced yesterday that he would step down in 2028; Lee said he thanked Zhang for his contributions to HKU and expressed confidence that the University Council would handle the recruitment well. (File photo)

Wong Kim-fai's resignation: no by-election for now, priority given to ensuring the smooth conduct of the next three elections

Legislative Council member Wong Kim-fai was arrested last month on suspicion of drink-driving and resigned from his seat earlier this month. Attention from the community has focused on whether a by-election will be held. Secretary for Constitutional and Mainland Affairs Sharon Shu earlier indicated that the timing was rather tight. Asked again today about the by-election, Lee said that three important elections would be held in the coming 18 months, including the Election Committee elections in November this year, the Chief Executive election in March next year, and the District Council elections before the end of next year. He said that for any election, the Electoral Affairs Commission would consider comprehensive factors, including human resources, venue arrangements, the setting up of polling stations, and the procurement and delivery of election supplies, taking into account overall work arrangements according to actual circumstances, as well as the relative necessity of each election.

Lee added that once the Election Committee elections are completed in November this year, the new term would begin on 1 February next year, to perform its role in the relevant elections. He believed that 'compared to a by-election for a single vacant LegCo seat, in terms of timing, workload and relative necessity, priority should be given to ensuring these three elections are well run.'

Wong Kim-fai resigned over a drink-driving charge, and attention from various sectors has focused on whether a by-election will be held for the vacant seat. Lee said priority should be given to ensuring the smooth conduct of the next three elections, while LegCo President Starry Lee said she respected the assessments of the Chief Executive and the Electoral Affairs Commission.

Asked whether the reduction in the number of members would affect LegCo's work, and whether she had spoken to Xia Baolong, Starry Lee said she understood and respected the assessments of the Chief Executive and the Electoral Affairs Commission, pointing out that as an important working partner of the government, LegCo would certainly first cooperate in and support the proper execution of a series of important tasks, including the first Five-Year Plan and the Policy Address. She added that although there had been changes in the Legislative Council, with only 89 members remaining, she 'believes every member will understand the need to take an extra step, to support and share the burden with one another more, because of the new situation arising from unpredictable changes', saying that all members would give their all, and that with the joint efforts of the 89 members, the functions of the whole Council would continue to be fulfilled as in the past.

No response on whether the Huanggang Port will commence operation before 1 October

The relevant bill for the Hong Kong side of the new Huanggang Port was passed earlier by the Legislative Council, and together with the related subsidiary legislation will come into effect on 31 July, but the date for the commencement of cross-boundary clearance has yet to be announced. When asked whether the port would be able to officially open before 1 October, Lee did not give a direct answer, saying he understood that everyone was very concerned about the port, and that after the establishment of the Hong Kong port area on 31 July, the governments of Hong Kong and Shenzhen would carry out operational tests for the port's operation, including system, installation and traffic stress tests, stressing that work on the installation, facilities, testing of operations and drills at the port is being pushed forward at full speed, with the goal of completing the work as soon as possible and opening it to the public at an early date, and that an announcement would be made once a decision had been taken.
